# Block 13: preliminary comparison across tag versions {#sec-block-13}

Block 13 compares DocuScope tags across four versions, to see how far zoning and the error rules change the picture. It reads `how_tags.parquet`, which block 12 saves with each tag's zone and rule matches. The results are preliminary. The checked rules remain untested, and the sender groups use a provisional rule.

| Version | Tags | Emails |
|---|---:|---:|
| Raw | 174,765 | 6,055 |
| Authored zone | 142,695 | 5,976 |
| Cleaned (authored zone, fixed-rule matches removed) | 141,311 | 5,923 |
| Upper bound (authored zone, all rule matches removed) | 134,529 | 5,923 |

## Category shares {#sec-block-13-shares}

The overall profile holds. Narrative, Positive and Interactive remain the three largest categories, and most shares move by less than one percentage point between the raw and cleaned versions. Two categories shrink sharply. Strategic falls by 37% relative to its raw share, as "task force" (2,694 tags) leaves with signatures and "research" drops from 3,334 tags to 512. Negative falls by 22%, as disclaimer wording leaves the authored zone. FirstPerson, Future and MetadiscourseInteractive rise by 15 to 19%, since boilerplate no longer dilutes them.

## Phrases {#sec-block-13-phrases}

Most categories rest on a few formulas. The ten most frequent phrases cover 82% of MetadiscourseCohesive tags, and "hesitate to" accounts for about half of Uncertainty. Strategic changes most, from 60% coverage by its ten most frequent phrases in the raw version to 31% after cleaning.

Misreadings survive cleaning. Positive counts "agreement" (959 tags), Interactive counts "email" (1,160), Inquiry counts "review" (473) and "assay" (280), and the most frequent ConfidenceHedged phrases, "we can" and "i can", state capability. These need rules before any further analysis.

## Sender groups {#sec-block-13-groups}

Block 13 assigns each email to CITF when the sender's domain matches `covid19immunitytaskforce.ca` or the sender's emails span five or more study IDs, and to study teams otherwise. CITF holds 3,477 emails from 30 senders and study teams hold 2,579 emails from 438 senders.

Cleaning changes the comparison between the groups. The raw gaps in Negative, Strategic and Positive come from disclaimers, signatures and the CITF name, and they shrink or reverse once those leave. After cleaning, CITF writes more Interactive and Contingent text, and study teams write more Narrative and FirstPerson text.

The grouping needs three corrections. echosign.com is an automated e-signature service and belongs in `automated_senders`. Maelstrom (349 emails) sits with CITF, and Statistics Canada (180 emails) sits with study teams, and both placements need a decision. Pooled shares can also reflect a few prolific senders, so each sender's shares need checking before the gaps are read as differences between groups.
